title: Is this… personal character development? #themusicman #broadway #hugh...
transcript: yesterday I did something that I didn't think I was going to do, and that was go see The Music Man on Broadway. now, this is the last musical of the twenty one, twenty two season that I hadn't seen, and it's closing this week. so I've been debating all week about whether or not I wanted to rush it. but I did not wanna get in line at 5 am for a show that really, frankly, I never wanted to see in the first place. yesterday at 1245 p m. I arrived in Times Square. my plan was to go to TKTS to get beautiful noise tickets. but as I got off the subway at 49th and looked to my right and saw the Winter Garden sign, I figured, why not let's just go to the box office, see what they have. and they in fact had a single mezzanine ticket for a hundred and $29, which is more than I wanted to pay. but I was about to pay 90 to go see a beautiful noise anyway. so I figured, fuck it, let's do it now. if you followed me for a long time, you know that this is a production I did not think we need of a musical that I do not like, period. and of course, there's the rooting of it all. but at this point I figured if I don't buy this ticket, somebody else is. and it's not like me talking about it. is going to convince anybody else to go see the show. it closes in 4 days. you know what? I had 1t of fun. now, all the criticisms of the show have already been said. Hugh Jackman can't really sing the role cut, and foster's vocal type doesn't really fit the character, but I kind of really loved her interpretation of Marion. the shippupy rewrites are weird and bizarre, and I don't understand them, but at the end of the day, everybody on this stage freaking loves performing this show, and I loved watching them perform it. while from a financial standpoint, I still don't love what this revival did, by increasing ticket prices and really just being a cash cow, but in a season where stuff is closing pretty much, surely I don't hate the idea of bringing in a star to do a year long revival just to make money, while also simultaneously hiring a bunch of people, including 1t of Broadway debuts. and considering all of the tourists that this show brought in that would then end up going to go see other Broadway shows, I think ultimately, my stance on revivals like this one has changed. I don't think I'm opposed to just bringing in a revival for a year, casting a big name that's gonna sell tickets, and helping revive this industry of Broadway that is, frankly, at this point in time, kind of struggling. and while I really don't love the show a lot, of people really do. and getting to see that and see a production that they really love is kind of heartwarming. I love people being in love with theater more than I hate the music, man. and if you have a mini horse and kids throwing books across the stage, I'm gonna have fun. so ultimately, I'm glad I saw this, and I'm glad that at the end of the day, I kind of had a change of heart.
